plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Ume are among the first trees to flower each year. Their bare, dark branches are covered in small, five-petaled blossoms with a sweet, spicy fragrance. The flowers are often seen against late-winter chill, which makes them a symbol of resilience.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early January to early March in the earliest-flowering gardens, with the main season later in colder regions
plants.location: Atami, Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan (Atami Plum Garden)
plants.funFact: Ume fruit is pickled into umeboshi and steeped in liqueur to make umeshu. The tree has been prized in East Asia for well over a thousand years, and poets there often celebrated it before the cherry.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: This evergreen shrub has glossy, deep-green leaves. Its blooms look like perfect rosettes of satin petals around a boss of golden stamens. They appear in the cold months, when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March in the wild, with cultivated varieties flowering from late autumn through spring
plants.location: Coastal woodlands and gardens of Japan, Korea and southern China
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Camellia oil, pressed from the seeds, has long been used in Japan as a hair and skin care oil.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers sit on tall, slender stems above fountains of strap-like leaves. In midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere they form blue-violet globes that hum with visiting bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly November to February, which covers midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South Africa, widely grown in gardens across Australia and other Southern Hemisphere regions
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'. It has become so successful outside its homeland that it is considered a weed in parts of Australia.
